answer: The pearl multiplier is published, charged in garden, and atlas lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 1162 identities would post 2350 proofs and burn roughly 18 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
